findings.claim: The observed landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate contrast over the full window (0.0-0.49) is non-monotone: it rises from about -0.37 z at t=0 to a peak near +1.64 z around t=0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at t=0.49, with 4 sign changes in the observed-node linear rate and polynomial_accepted=false. This is a changing contrast, not a stationary target.

Across all 20 landmark soft-mass features, whole-window mean z is small in magnitude (|whole_window_z| < ~0.65) while every feature shows multiple sign changes and strong_sign_conflicts, so the window does not support a single signed global direction.

The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the coordinate features are predicted_endpoint_world_A_features, i.e. untyped coordinate proxies, not physical energies.

hypotheses.direction: test earlier robust response to large residuals then baseline curvature, at fixed dose and fixed teachers
hypotheses.falsifier: If C1_robust_to_base produces no change in the compiled delta table or no change in the realized trace relative to the constant-curvature control C2, the time-dependent curvature hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate contrast (observed-node linear rate z) over the full observed score window
hypotheses.statement: A time-dependent curvature schedule (registered C1_robust_to_base: delta 0.5 -> 0.75 -> 1.0 over knots 0/0.5/1, dose fixed at 1, blend 0) is a candidate to test, because the observed landmark_00_soft_mass contrast is non-monotone with a mid-window peak and late-window decline, so a single constant curvature may not match the changing contrast.

hypotheses.direction: retain constant curvature as the reference; do not infer a data-derived knot from the near-zero whole-window mean
hypotheses.falsifier: If C2 and C1 yield indistinguishable realized traces and quality, the time-dependent curvature edit is not justified.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass whole-window mean z and realized trace under C2
hypotheses.statement: The constant-curvature control C2 (delta 0.75 at all knots, dose 1, blend 0) is the appropriate baseline against which any time-dependent curvature claim must be compared, because the observed landmark_00_soft_mass whole-window mean z is small and the curve does not by itself establish a reproducible stage boundary.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves and trend tables were read.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in role input; selection/survival and coordinate contrasts are not evidence of final affinity improvement.
Coordinate features are untyped predicted_endpoint_world_A proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
The observed rate sign changes are diagnostics of changing contrast, not permission to reverse the affinity objective or to define an absolute coordinate target.
